LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: THE FAMILY SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: family, relative, care-giver, sibling, orphan, 
Topic 11.1.1: Pronunciation and Vocabulary

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Pronunciation and Vocabulary. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Today we shall learn how to pronounce sounds and words correctly.

In today’s lesson, you shall learn how to pronounce sounds and words correctly. Learner, why should we pronounce words correctly? Answer when you hear the Good learner. We should pronounce words correctly to communicate well. Communicating is speaking and listening to one another. Others are able to hear us clearly. A simile is used to compare one thing to another different thing. L earner, I will read a short story. Listen carefully as I read. Identify all the similes in the story. The story is called ‘Free from Malaria’ When Jane’s mother went to the hospital, she was as afraid as a grasshopper. Her skin had become as pale as death and she had a bad cough. Her blood was as red as beetroot. The doctor took part of her blood to the laboratory. He brought the results as fast as a deer. She had malaria and was given two injections. Jane’s mother went home feeling as happy as a lark. Let me repeat the story When Jane’s mother went to the hospital, she was as afraid as a grasshopper. Her skin had become as pale as death and she had a bad cough. Her blood was as red as beetroot. The doctor took part of her blood to the laboratory. He brought the results as fast as a deer. She had malaria and was given two injections. Jane’s mother went home feelin as happy as a lark. Thank you learner for listening. Now I want you to identify all the similes in the story very good learner. The similes are: As afraid as a grasshopper. As pale as death. As red as beetroot As fast as a deer. And finally As happy as a lark. learner did you hear the sound /s/ in the similes? Give two more examples of similes using the sound /s/. Thank you learner, the following are more examples. As quiet as a grave. As busy as a bee. learner, now I want you to say the words with the following sounds after me. Say the words after the /s/- virus /z/-easier /h/-huge /f/-affect, I am going to read you a poem. Listen carefully. Write down words with the sounds /s/-/z/-/h/-/f/. -‘gh’ Here I go AIDS, I have heard enough of you, You will not destroy our children, We have found a tough weapon against you, Exercise, balanced diet and medicine, You are no longer a puzzle. Thank you learner. I hope you have written down the following sounds and words; /s/- destroy, exercise, medicine /f/- ‘gh’-enough, tough /h/-have /z/-puzzle. Learner, I want you to give more examples of words with the sounds /s/-/h/-/f/-/z/. Thank you learner, I hope you gave examples as follows: /s/-sick, signs, skin /f/-infect, cough, rough, /h/-headache, huge, who /z/-sneeze, boys, zip, Learner, this is your homework. With the help of your parent or gurdian, try to practice pronouncing more words with the sounds we have learnt today. I hope you enjoyed the lesson. That’s the end of our lesson today. Your radio teacher was Joyce Agik.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Pronunciation and Vocabulary means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
2. Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
3. Learning materials: ENGLISH_GRADE_4___PROG_10 pronounce sounds
4. Revise with the quiz now.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
